messages:
maria: quick follow-up from the egress retry RFC — sketching a smaller scope proposal to unblock the gateway/edge split. TL;DR: make the egress retry window adaptive at the edge but keep retry *policy* decision (when to retry vs failover) in gateway control plane. thoughts?

ajay: can you expand "adaptive"? do you mean dynamically sizing the window based on in-flight tokens / client deadline? :thinking_face:
maria: yes. two knobs: 1) window duration (ms) tuned by observed egress queue length & downstream latency distribution, 2) max buffered bytes per connection (so we don't OOM during large streaming responses). gateway still decides whether a request is retriable. edge just manages holding/resuming streams.
sam: +1 for separating policy vs buffering. one risk: if edge silently buffers longer than client deadline we end up with phantom latency and confusing metrics. need clear observability hooks.
clare: agree with sam. also need explicit boundary around side-effects. if a retried request is non-idempotent, gateway policy should veto retry attempts entirely. edge should expose attempt metadata so the gateway can reconcile.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for edge-proxy v2.3 with env flag EDGE_ADAPTIVE_WINDOW=true scheduled at 2026-04-02T09:00Z
maria: thanks. thoughts on an implementation sketch:

- on request arrival, gateway annotates request with header `x-rw-retry-policy: <policy-id>` and `x-rw-client-deadline-ms`.
- edge keeps a small in-memory sliding window per upstream (configurable) and tracks: inflight_count, avg_upstream_lat_ms, queued_bytes.
- when an upstream hiccup happens, edge will: 1) decide whether to attempt a resume based on header policy+rate limits (gateway tells permitted attempts) 2) if permitted, hold the connection for up to adaptive_window_ms = clamp(k * avg_upstream_lat_ms, min, max) 3) if client deadline - now < safe_margin -> short-circuit to gateway fallback (failover).

example header flow:
```
X-RW-Retry-Policy: canary-id-7
X-RW-Client-Deadline-MS: 15000
X-RW-Attempt: 1/3
```

ajay: i like the adaptive_window formula. what's k and safe_margin? also how do we surface that the edge held the stream so analytics don't attribute latency to upstream?
maria: propose k=3 by default (covers tail spikes), min=30ms, max=5s. safe_margin = 250ms (plus client transport RTT estimate) — conservative so gateway can trigger failover. for telemetry, edge emits a short event when it transitions to "holding" and another when it resumes/aborts, including attempt id. those events are batched to console and tagged with policy-id.
sam: we should also record a boolean "side_effects_disallowed" derived from policy header so edge won't buffer on non-idempotent ops. gateway must set that.
clare: operational question: what if edge restarts while holding a stream? do we leak state? suggestion: make holding ephemeral only; on restart edge emits an abort to client and sets retryable=true so gateway can reissue or failover. document that as a constraint.
maria: agreed. holding is best-effort; state is not durable. if edge loses state -> abort with `x-rw-edge-abort: restart-loss` and gateway uses its routing policy to decide next step.
infra-bot: infra-note: this will touch the connection manager state machine. add health-checks for queued_bytes growth.
ajay: perf question: do we need per-request KV for windows or can we aggregate per-upstream? per-request is heavier.
maria: aggregate per-upstream for sizing, per-request for safety checks (client deadline, side-effect flag). should be fine.
sam: can we add a small config example for ops? helps SREs.
maria: sure:
```
edge.retry.adaptive_window.enabled = true
edge.retry.adaptive_window.k = 3
edge.retry.adaptive_window.min_ms = 30
edge.retry.adaptive_window.max_ms = 5000
edge.retry.max_buffer_bytes_per_conn = 4MB
edge.retry.safe_margin_ms = 250
```

clare: lgtm. one more: showback for cost — when edge holds a stream it still consumes socket and CPU, mark held_time on billing metrics so Dedicated customers aren't surprised.
maria: good call. will add telemetry + billing tag `held_ms`.

next steps: I'll draft a short RFC addendum that: 1) defines headers, 2) outlines state transitions (normal -> holding -> resume/abort), 3) lists operational knobs and observability signals, 4) documents failure modes (edge restart, buffer exhaustion). tagging @ajay @sam @clare for review before I merge. :memo:
ajay: will review today.
sam: quick +1, will test in canary.
clare: will verify SLO implications and billing tagging.
infra-bot: canary scheduled window acknowledged.
